To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

simple and complex FRBs in primary visual cortex generate γ oscillations spontaneously and in response both to current injection and to visual stimulation, and that the γ oscillations in simple FRB cells are driven primarily by synaptic inputs rather than by intrinsic membrane properties.

FRB neurons in primary visual cortex are distributed throughout the six cortical layers and are divided into two subgroups, simple and complex, that generate γ frequency oscillations in response either to depolarizing or to hyperpolarizing current injection.

simple and complex fast rhythmic bursting (chattering) cells in the primary somatosensory cortex (S1) of mice are distributed throughout all six cortical layers and that both simple and complex cells generate γ oscillations in their membrane potentials (Vm) in response to current pulses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation and function of fast rhythmic bursting cells in the visual cortex.
the mechanisms of oscillations in the brain and the role of these oscillations for information processing.
the role of oscillatory activity in visual processing and its relation to attention.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
γ oscillations in visual cortex are generated in large part in the thalamocortical system, with the cortex amplifying and distributing them.

γ oscillations in FRB cells are not generated by intrinsic mechanisms but are driven by synaptic inputs, and the FRB cells may play a role in the generation of oscillations in the corticothalamus loop.

the present study provides evidence for the first time of a unique population of cortical neurons that are intrinsically capable of generating γ band oscillations and that can be recruited to participate in sensory-evoked cortical activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the simple and complex FRBs are two different subtypes of FRBs, which are different from the other cortical cells.

we have found that the FRB cells in primary visual cortex are distributed throughout all layers, and that both simple and complex types of these cells can generate γ oscillations in their responses to depolarizing currents, and that only simple FRB neurons show an increase in γ oscillation power in response to visual stimuli.
the FRB cells in primary visual cortex (V1) are distributed throughout all layers and are capable of generating γ band oscillations in response either to current injection or visual stimulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FRB cells, which are found throughout the neocortex and thalamus, are not pacemakers but rather are amplifiers of γ oscillations.
the γ band oscillations in visual cortex are not only generated spontaneously but also can be evoked by sensory stimulation.

FRB cells are a unique type of cortical neuron that generate high frequency bursts of action potentials in response to current injection or synaptic activation, and that they are present in all cortical layers, including layer 6.
